subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
passage:
I'm Yamini, and when Vaibhav told me he'd got the internship at the software firm, I said "Wow, that's amazing!" and hugged him in the corridor, my face smiling on its own. Inside I felt small. I had applied to the same firm and heard nothing.

That night I texted him "So proud of you 🎉" and meant it, mostly. Then I lay awake admitting to myself, only to myself, that I was jealous. What surprised me was that the envy pointed at something: I didn't actually want that firm, I wanted work where I build things, and I'd been applying by default.

Two days later I told Vaibhav I'd been a little jealous and was still glad for him. He laughed and said he'd been jealous of my grades for a year.

qa.q: What did Yamini text Vaibhav that night?
qa.a: "So proud of you", with a party emoji.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling behind the smile in the corridor, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Small and jealous. The smile felt automatic, and Yamini later lay awake admitting the envy privately.

qa.q: How did Yamini use the envy well?
qa.a: Yamini admitted it privately, congratulated Vaibhav honestly and used the feeling to see what work Yamini actually wanted.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav react to the confession, and what does that show?
qa.a: He laughed and said he had been jealous of Yamini's grades for a year, so the honesty made the friendship feel more equal. 🙂

grounding: A friend gets the offer while Yamini has heard nothing; Yamini smiles while feeling small, admits the envy privately, congratulates honestly and clarifies what Yamini wants.

subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
passage:
Placement cell note, final-year batch, 4 December
Sonali got the design-firm offer this morning, and the whole batch crowded around her. I noticed Gurpreet, her closest friend, hugging her with a wide smile, then standing at the back afterwards, twisting her ID card strap.
Later Gurpreet came to my desk to ask about the next drive. Halfway through, she said, "Can I be honest? I'm happy for her and I also feel really small. We applied to the same firm." She looked embarrassed saying it.
I told her envy is common and can be useful; it often points at what we want. We looked at her portfolio together, and she said what she envied was not the firm but Sonali's confidence in interviews. We booked two mock interviews for next week.
On her way out she stopped by Sonali's bench and said quietly, "You earned it. Treat me to chai?" Sonali laughed and said yes.

qa.q: What was Gurpreet twisting at the back of the crowd?
What mix of feelings did Gurpreet admit to?
qa.a: Happiness for Sonali and a feeling of being really small, a quiet envy she was embarrassed to say aloud.

qa.q: How did the placement officer help Gurpreet use the envy?
qa.a: By treating it as a pointer to what she wants, reviewing her portfolio with her, and booking two mock interviews to build her interview confidence.

qa.q: How might Sonali see Gurpreet's "You earned it"?
qa.a: As warm and sincere; she laughs and agrees to chai, likely unaware of the struggle behind it.

grounding: Shows envy at a friend's offer, admitting it privately, congratulating honestly and using it to clarify what one wants.

subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
passage:
Friday
Results came out. Ayesha topped the class with 9.4. I got 7.1. She came running to show me her phone, and I smiled so hard my face hurt and said, "Of course you did!"
Then at the canteen, when Imtiaz said "Ayesha's crazy smart", I opened my mouth to say "she's just good at mugging up". I stopped. That's not even true. She explains things to me every week.
Truth: I'm jealous. I feel like I'm running behind everyone. There, I wrote it.
So what do I actually want? Not her marks exactly. I want to stop leaving everything to the last week. I want to understand circuits the way she does.
I messaged her: "Seriously proud of you. Can you do one circuits session with me on Sunday? I'll bring samosas." She said yes with three exclamation marks.
— Vijay

qa.q: How did Vijay feel while smiling at Ayesha's result?
qa.a: Jealous and small, like running behind everyone, while still smiling so hard it hurt.

qa.q: How did Vijay turn the envy into something useful?
qa.a: By admitting it in the diary, naming what was really wanted (steady study and understanding circuits), and asking Ayesha for a Sunday session.

qa.q: How might Ayesha see Vijay's message?
qa.a: As real pride from a friend; her three exclamation marks show she is happy to help.

grounding: Illustrates feeling small at a friend's success, resisting the urge to belittle it, and using the envy to see what one wants.
